whatsHappening.background: Syria’s crisis began in 2011 when anti-government protests were met with violent repression, escalating into a long war involving the Assad government, opposition forces, ISIS, foreign militaries, and regional powers. Assad was removed from power in December 2024, but insecurity, damaged infrastructure, displacement, and humanitarian needs continue to shape daily life.

parties.description: Ruled Syria for decades and violently repressed the 2011 uprising.

parties.name: Opposition / New Authorities
parties.description: Anti-Assad forces and successor authorities now shaping Syria’s transition.

parties.name: ISIS
parties.description: Militant group that expanded during the war and still exploits insecurity.

parties.name: Foreign Powers
parties.description: Russia, Iran, Turkey, the U.S., Israel, and others influenced the war.

timeline.description: Anti-government protests begin and are violently repressed.
ISIS expands as the war fragments across Syria.
Assad is removed from power after opposition advances.
Needs remain high during an unstable transition.

civilianImpact.experiences: After more than a decade of war, civilians continue to face displacement, damaged homes, weakened health care, economic hardship, and explosive remnants of war. The political shift created cautious hope, but recovery is still slowed by insecurity and destroyed services.

howToHelp.summary: This page explains how Syria moved from the 2011 uprising into a long conflict and ongoing humanitarian crisis.

learnMore.text: The crisis continues because political change has not immediately repaired displacement, hunger, damaged services, or explosive hazards.

whatsHappening.background: Syria remains one of the world’s largest humanitarian emergencies. Families continue to live with displacement, hunger, unsafe water, interrupted schooling, damaged hospitals, and the threat of landmines and unexploded ordnance.

parties.name: Displaced Families
parties.description: Millions remain displaced inside Syria or across the region.

parties.name: Children
parties.description: Many face malnutrition, missed school, trauma, and protection risks.

parties.name: Returnees
parties.description: Families often return to damaged communities without full services.

parties.name: Camp Communities
parties.description: Many still depend on aid for shelter, food, water, and health care.

timeline.description: People internally displaced by the start of 2026.
Children under five suffering from wasting.

image.alt: Before and after damage in Syria

civilianImpact.experiences: Children in Syria have grown up with conflict as a constant. Damage to schools, weak health systems, unsafe water, economic collapse, and explosive remnants of war increase risks of illness, child labor, child marriage, and long-term trauma.

image.alt: Aerial view of the Za'atari refugee camp

howToHelp.summary: Civilian recovery is complicated by damaged infrastructure, poverty, displacement, and explosive ordnance that threatens children’s safety and access to schools and services.

learnMore.text: The crisis affects health, nutrition, education, protection, and safe return for families across Syria.

image.alt: Aerial view of the Za'atari refugee camp

whatsHappening.background: Support is most effective when it goes to organizations already delivering food, shelter, education, protection, health services, and refugee support. Humanitarian aid remains essential because returns alone do not mean families are returning to safe or fully functioning communities.

parties.name: UNICEF
parties.description: Supports children with health, nutrition, education, water, and protection.

parties.name: UNHCR
parties.description: Supports refugees, returnees, shelter, and protection services.

parties.name: WFP
parties.description: Provides food assistance for vulnerable households.

parties.name: IRC / MSF
parties.description: Support protection, recovery, and medical care where access is possible.

timeline.description: Support trusted relief groups working with Syrians.
Use verified humanitarian updates, not rumors.
Keep attention on civilians and refugees.

civilianImpact.experiences: Helping Syria means funding food, clean water, medical treatment, education, child protection, and support for displaced families and returnees trying to rebuild their lives.
